Tables returned by the reads

Source: R/results.R
soil_table.Rd

Reads such as soil_observations() return a soil_table: a data.frame (or an sf object, with sf's class kept in front of data.frame) whose class starts with "soil_table", with two attributes:

Usage

# S3 method for class 'soil_table'
x[...]

# S3 method for class 'soil_table'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'soil_table'
print(x, n = getOption("soilhub.print_rows", 10), ...)

# S3 method for class 'soil_table'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

x, object

A soil_table. Client-side: not sent to the API.

...

As for a data frame ([); unused otherwise. Client-side: not sent to the API.

row.names, optional

Unused (the row names are kept). Client-side: not sent to the API.

n

Rows to print. Client-side: not sent to the API.

Details

  • soil_metadata, read with soil_metadata(): the request sent, the request ids of the pages, whether the read is complete, the API warnings, the typing of the variable columns (soil_columns()), the view and the revised rules applied (soil_revised_rules()), the first-layer vocabulary (soil_first_layer()), the catalog rows of the datasets (for soil_citations());

  • soil_layout: "wide", "long", "features", "values" or "health".

Subsetting with [ keeps the class and the attributes; as.data.frame() drops them (and the sf class: the geometry column stays). Rows are in the API's order (the stable order of the pages).

Printing shows a two-line header (counts, datasets, view and layer; warnings and the helpers to use) and the first getOption("soilhub.print_rows", 10) rows, list columns as <list>. summary() shows the typing of the variable columns, the rows per dataset and, with view = "revised", the rules applied with their counts.

See also

Other results: soil_columns(), soil_first_layer(), soil_flags(), soil_markings(), soil_metadata(), soil_revised_rules()
